# A Short Graph Walk

**Claim.** If a finite sequence of neighbor steps connects $x$ to $t$, then the simple graph generated by the neighbor relation has a walk from $x$ to $t$ of length strictly less than $|V|$.

**Proof.** Induct along the given finite sequence of neighbor steps to show that $x$ and $t$ are reachable in the generated simple graph. A reflexive step gives reachability immediately. For an initial neighbor step, if its endpoints coincide, discard that step and use the remainder; otherwise it is an edge of the generated simple graph, and adjoining it to the reachable remainder gives reachability. Reachability provides a walk; removing repetitions yields a simple path, whose length is strictly less than the number of vertices.
